overview.title: The Art & Science of Mountaineering
overview.definition: Mountaineering, or alpinism, is the sport, craft, and art of climbing mountains. Unlike standard trekking, it encompasses technical travel over snow, glaciers, steep rock, and ice in harsh, high-altitude environments where self-reliance, physical stamina, and objective hazard management are paramount.

corePillars.title: Technical Competence
corePillars.description: Mastery of rope work, anchor building, ice axe and crampon mechanics, glacier rescue systems, and route finding in pathless terrain.

corePillars.title: Physiological Endurance & Acclimatization
corePillars.description: Understanding high-altitude physiology, oxygen deprivation, metabolic pacing, and the biological necessity of step-wise acclimatization.

corePillars.title: Meteorological & Terrain Acumen
corePillars.description: Reading isobaric maps, predicting localized katabatic windstorms, evaluating snowpack avalanche stability, and anticipating rock/ice fall.

corePillars.title: Ethical Stewardship
corePillars.description: Adhering to clean climbing, Leave No Trace (LNT), respect for indigenous mountain communities, and leaving summits unmarked.

ethics.summary: Minimize the use of permanent pitons and bolts; employ removable active and passive protection (cams, nuts, ice screws).
Fair pay, proper gear, high-altitude insurance, and equal respect for local porters, High Altitude Helpers, and Sherpa guides.

ethics.principle: Leave No Waste in the Death Zone
ethics.summary: Complete pack-out of oxygen canisters, human waste, fixed ropes, and camp remnants from high camps.
Summits are optional; returning home safely is mandatory. Prioritizing human life over any summit objective.
